name: Anouk Aimée

family_context_summary: Born to two actors: father Henry Murray (Henri Dreyfus) was Jewish, mother Geneviève Sorya was Catholic. She was raised Catholic and later converted to Judaism. The family was part of the Parisian theatre and film world.

evidence_summary: Anouk Aimée was born to two working actors in Paris and was discovered at 14 by director Henri Calef, who cast her in La Maison sous la mer (1947). By 17, she starred in Les Amants de Vérone (1949), a role written specifically for her by poet Jacques Prévert, who also gave her the surname Aimée. Both parents' acting careers provided direct domain immersion and industry connections that facilitated her extraordinarily early start. She studied dance at the Marseille Opera and dramatic art with Andrée Bauer-Thérond.

current_position: Died on June 18, 2024 in Paris at age 92; final film appearance was in 2019. Best known for A Man and a Woman (1966), La Dolce Vita (1960), and 8½ (1963).

name: Alexander Almetov

He joined CSKA Moscow at 18 and the USSR national team at 19, forming one of the most dominant lines in Soviet hockey history with Loktev and Aleksandrov.

name: Didier Raoult
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; he dropped out of high school, spent two years at sea, then obtained his baccalauréat at 20 and entered medical school. He graduated from medical school in 1978 at age 26, but his major research contributions came later.

family_context_summary: Born in Dakar, French West Africa (present-day Senegal). Father was a military doctor (colonel) from Brittany; mother was a nurse from Marseille. evidence_summary: Raoult had a strong family medical tradition—his father was a military doctor and his maternal great-great-grandfather was a physician with 260 publications—but his path was unconventional.
